The algorithm is given a set of inputs and corresponding outputs, and it learns to map the inputs to the outputs. For example, a supervised learning algorithm could be trained on a dataset of images and their corresponding labels (e.g. "cat" or "dog"). The algorithm would learn to recognize the features of each image and classify it as either a cat or a dog. Unsupervised learning is a type of machine learning where the algorithm is trained on unlabeled data. The algorithm is given a set of inputs and it learns to identify patterns or clusters in the data. For example, an unsupervised learning algorithm could be trained on a dataset of customer purchase history. The algorithm would learn to identify patterns in the data, such as which products are frequently purchased together or which customers have similar purchase histories. Reinforcement learning is a type of machine learning where the algorithm is trained on a set of actions and their corresponding rewards. The algorithm learns to take actions that maximize the reward. For example, a reinforcement learning algorithm could be trained on a game of chess. The algorithm would learn to make moves that maximize its chances of winning the game. Real-world examples of each type of machine learning include: 1. Supervised learning: Image recognition, speech recognition, and fraud detection. 2.
